paragraphs: Friend, listen to this. Before Bezalel picks up a single tool, God has already called him by name and filled him "with the Spirit of God, with skill, ability, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship" (Exodus 31:3). The skill comes from God. Then God gives Oholiab to help him, and says He has "given skill to all the craftsmen" (Exodus 31:6). So nobody builds alone, and nobody builds on their own power.

Now look where the Sabbath lands. Right after all that building, God says, "Surely you must keep My Sabbaths" (Exodus 31:13). Even the holiest work in the world has to stop for a day of "complete rest, holy to the LORD" (Exodus 31:15). God says the Sabbath is a sign so that they "may know that I am the LORD who sanctifies you" (Exodus 31:13). I think that means the work doesn't make you holy. HE does, and I needed to hear that, because I'm a stamper who wants to keep stamping.

Here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery today, baker. God gives the gifts, and God gives the helpers. Then God gives the rest, and He points to His own example: "in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, but on the seventh day He rested and was refreshed" (Exodus 31:17). Do your work with joy, and when it's time to rest, REST. The One who made you is the One doing the making holy. The story isn't over, either, because there's more waiting for Moses at the bottom of that mountain.
